Heard Mr. M. P. S. Bhatia, learned counsel for the appellant.

Also heard Mr. N. K. Jaiswal, learned Dy.
Govt. Advocate, appearing for the respondent/State on the instant application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail I.A. No. 01.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.

It is contended that there is no legally admissible evidence regarding the age of the victim and that the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt,
thereby entitling the appellant to acquittal.
He further submits that the prosecution has not examined any trustworthy and independent witness in support of its case.

It is also argued that no injury was found on the body of the victim, particularly on her private parts, and that the MLC does not give any definite opinion regarding the commission of sexual assault.
There has been an unexplained delay of six months in lodging the FIR, which casts serious doubt on the prosecution story.
He would further submit that the victim has also lodged a report against the other accused persons, in respect of which separate offences were registered.

In those cases, the other co-accused persons have been convicted by the learned trial Court, but another accused, Devendra Usendi, was acquitted by this Court in CRA No. 1040/2024, decided on 11.04.2025 and the sentence awarded to accused Sanjay Kachlam has been suspended, and he has been released on bail in CRA No.
. Thus, the report lodged by the victim against the present appellant is also suspicious.
The appellant was on bail during trial and has not misused the liberty granted to him.
Presently the appellant in jail since 26.07.2024 and final adjudication of the case will take it own time

, therefore,
he may be enlarge on bail.
As per the submission of the learned State counsel, the notice issued to the complainant has been served.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes and have submitted she was subjected to forceful sexual intercourse by the appellant and as per the medical evidence, the victim is reported to be pregnant.

The prosecution has successfully established the commission of offences under Sections 366, 376(2)
(n), and 376(3) IPC through the credible and consistent testimony of the victim.
Neither the alleged absence of injuries nor the delay in lodging the FIR undermines the prosecution case.

The question of the accused age was duly considered by the learned trial Court in accordance with law, therefore,
in view of the evidence available on record, the appellant is not entitled for bail.

sentences.text: Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties, the nature of the allegations, the evidence of the victim PW-1 as well as the evidence regarding her age and that she being minor on the date of incident subjected to rape by the appellant, we consider this not a fit case to grant bail to the appellant.
Accordingly, I.A. No. 01, filed by the appellant- Sampat Kashyap is rejected.
List this case for final hearing in due course.
